# Declaring a generic attribute in a Pydantic model that itself has a generic attribute breaks deserialisation of the declared class

### Description

I have models `X(BaseModel, Generic[T])` and `Y(BaseModel, Generic[T])`.  `X` has an attribute `y` of type `Y[T]`.  `Y` has an attribute `obj` of type `T`.  `C` is an empty class `C(BaseModel)`.

If I create `x = X[C](y=Y[C](obj=C())`, then `isinstance(x.y.obj, C)`.  If I serialise and deserialise this remains true.

However if I create a model that declares an attribute of type `X[C]`:

```
class PydanticModel(BaseModel):
  x: "X[C]"
```

the upon serialisation / deserialisation, the type of `x.y.obj` becomes a `dict`.  _Even if I don't use `PydanticModel` at all._


### Example Code

```Python
from typing import TypeVar, Generic

from pydantic import BaseModel

T = TypeVar("T")

def test_ser():
    class C(BaseModel):
        pass

    class X(BaseModel, Generic[T]):
        y: "Y[T]"

    class Y(BaseModel, Generic[T]):
        obj: T

    class PydanticModel(BaseModel): #<-- comment out this class and the test passes
        x: "X[C]"

    x = X[C](
        y=Y[C](obj=C()),
    )

    assert isinstance(x, X)
    assert isinstance(x.y, Y)
    assert isinstance(x.y.obj, C)

    j_c = x.model_dump_json()

    deser_c = X[C].model_validate_json(j_c)

    assert isinstance(deser_c, X)
    assert isinstance(deser_c.y, Y)
    assert isinstance(deser_c.y.obj, C) #<-- this line fails
```
